symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in the source vector u.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the lengths of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in the target vector g.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the lengths of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The ratio t/s minus one, the relative gap between the two lengths.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the lengths of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.meaning: A length-s vector of input values.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a length-$s$ source vector and $g$ a length-$t$ target vector.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: A length-t vector of output values.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a length-$s$ source vector and $g$ a length-$t$ target vector.

symbols.name: source index
symbols.meaning: An index of the entries of u, read modulo s.
symbols.quote: Entries of $u$ are indexed by $j$, entries of $g$ by $k$, and an index is read modulo the length, so $u_j=u_{j \bmod s}$ for every integer $j$.

symbols.name: target index
symbols.meaning: An index of the entries of g, read modulo t.
symbols.quote: Entries of $u$ are indexed by $j$, entries of $g$ by $k$, and an index is read modulo the length, so $u_j=u_{j \bmod s}$ for every integer $j$.

symbols.name: summation index
symbols.meaning: The index of the sum over all integers defining the entries of Nu.
symbols.quote: The same rule defines $\ell_h$ and $\beta_h$ for every integer $h$, which is the summation index used below.

symbols.name: length-s transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform on length-$s$ vectors and $P_s$ the coordinate permutation $(P_s u)_j=u_{tj}$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation $(P_s u)_j=u_{tj}$ on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform on length-$s$ vectors and $P_s$ the coordinate permutation $(P_s u)_j=u_{tj}$.

symbols.name: length-t transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform on length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_t g)_k=g_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation $(P_t g)_k=g_{-sk}$ on length-t vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_t g)_k=g_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: source Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The map from length-s to length-t vectors that gathers the entries of u near sk/t.
symbols.quote: Let $S$ and $T$ be the maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors given by

symbols.name: target Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The map from length-s to length-t vectors that spreads each entry of u over the targets near tj/s.
symbols.quote: Let $S$ and $T$ be the maps from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors given by

symbols.name: Gaussian width parameter
symbols.meaning: The integer parameter that sets the width of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The integer $\alpha$ sets the width of the Gaussian weights, which are bell-shaped functions of $j$ that decay quickly away from their centres.

symbols.name: nearest coordinate
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest tj/s, with ties rounded up, which is the coordinate selected for index j.
symbols.quote: For $0\le j<s$, let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, ties rounded up, and $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The offset tj/s minus its nearest integer, the amount by which the Gaussian weight is cancelled.
symbols.quote: For $0\le j<s$, let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, ties rounded up, and $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: diagonal factor
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying entry j by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The map $N=CTD$ from length-s to length-s vectors, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map on length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $I$ be the identity map on length-$s$ vectors, so $N-I$ collects the remaining terms.

symbols.name: error map
symbols.meaning: The error $I-N$, whose operator norm is small.
symbols.quote: Write $E=I-N$ for the error, so $N=I-E$.

symbols.name: output map
symbols.meaning: The linear map $DN^{-1}C$ from length-t to length-s vectors.
symbols.quote: Multiplying on the left by $N^{-1}$ and then by $D$ gives $P_sF_s=DN^{-1}C\,P_tF_tS$, which has the form $P_sF_s=BP_tF_tS$ with $B=DN^{-1}C$ a linear map.

symbols.name: Neumann index
symbols.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series $\sum_{r\ge0}E^r$.
symbols.quote: The Neumann series is the operator version of the geometric series, $\sum_{r\ge0}E^r$, with $r$ its summation index.

symbols.name: last partial-sum index
symbols.meaning: The last index of the partial sum $\sum_{r=0}^{R}E^r$.
symbols.quote: Let $R$ be the last index of a partial sum $\sum_{r=0}^{R}E^r$.

symbols.name: precision parameter
symbols.meaning: The integer precision parameter, greater than 100, in the hypotheses of the estimate.
symbols.quote: Here $p>100$ is an integer precision parameter, and the estimate applies when $\alpha$ is an integer with $2\le\alpha<p$, $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta>p/\alpha^4$.

symbols.name: coordinate selection
symbols.meaning: The map from length-t to length-s vectors that selects the coordinates $\ell_j$, so that each output entry copies one input entry.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, using Gaussian weights to move between the two sets of frequencies.
It replaces the transforms for the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of two integers by such transforms.
The error $E$ is measured in the [operator norm](operator-norm.md) for the maximum-modulus vector norm, and $\|E\|=\|N-I\|$.
